# Load packages

```{r, message=FALSE}
library("knitr")
library("tidyverse")
```

# Global options

```{r}
theme_set(theme_classic())

opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>",
               fig.show = "hold")

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
```

# EXPERIMENT 1 (Adult Norming)

## Read in the data

```{r}
# Use the local de-identified CSVs for the main study.
if (!file.exists(params$responses_file)) {
  stop("Save the main study's de-identified responses.csv at data/Norming/responses.csv, then knit again.",
       call. = FALSE)
}
if (!file.exists(params$demographics_file)) {
  stop("Save the main study's de-identified demographics.csv at data/Norming/demographics.csv, then knit again.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

df.exp1.data = read_csv(params$responses_file,
                       col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                       col_select = c(participant_id, study_key,
                                      experiment_version, mode, trial_role,
                                      item_id, property_text, selected_label))

df.exp1.demographics = read_csv(params$demographics_file,
                               col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                               col_select = c(participant_id, study_key, experiment_version, mode,
                                              age, gender, race, ethnicity))
```

## Wrangle

```{r}
categories = c("Behavioral", "Self-benefiting", "Ecological", "Human-benefiting")

# Use the categorization trials from the preregistered main study.
df.exp1.long = df.exp1.data %>%
  filter(study_key == params$study_key,
         experiment_version == params$experiment_version,
         mode == "production",
         trial_role == "response") %>%
  transmute(participant = participant_id,
            item_id,
            item = property_text,
            response = factor(selected_label, levels = categories))

n.participants = n_distinct(df.exp1.long$participant)
if (n.participants != params$expected_n) {
  stop(sprintf("Found %d main-study participants. Expected %d before making the figure.",
               n.participants, params$expected_n), call. = FALSE)
}

# Each participant should have exactly one judgment on every item.
items = df.exp1.long %>% distinct(item_id, item)
participant.items = df.exp1.long %>% count(participant, item_id)
participant.trials = df.exp1.long %>% count(participant)
stopifnot(!anyNA(df.exp1.long),
          all(str_detect(df.exp1.long$participant, "^P[0-9]{3,}$")),
          nrow(items) == 40L,
          n_distinct(items$item_id) == 40L,
          n_distinct(items$item) == 40L,
          all(participant.items$n == 1L),
          all(participant.trials$n == 40L))
```

## Demographics

```{r exp1-demographics}
df.exp1.demographics = df.exp1.demographics %>%
  filter(study_key == params$study_key,
         experiment_version == params$experiment_version,
         mode == "production") %>%
  select(participant_id, age, gender, race, ethnicity)

# Match the demographics rows to the same participants included in the analysis.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.exp1.demographics$participant_id),
          setequal(df.exp1.demographics$participant_id, participant.trials$participant))

age.reported = df.exp1.demographics %>%
  pull(age) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  as.numeric()

stopifnot(all(is.finite(age.reported)), all(between(age.reported, 18, 120)))

age.summary = tibble(
  Measure = "Age",
  Response = if (length(age.reported) > 1L) {
    sprintf("%.1f (SD %.1f), range %d–%d",
            mean(age.reported), sd(age.reported), min(age.reported), max(age.reported))
  } else if (length(age.reported) == 1L) {
    as.character(age.reported)
  } else {
    "No reported ages"
  },
  n = length(age.reported)
)

if (length(age.reported) < n.participants) {
  age.summary = bind_rows(age.summary,
                          tibble(Measure = "Age", Response = "Missing",
                                 n = n.participants - length(age.reported)))
}

category.summary = df.exp1.demographics %>%
  select(gender, race, ethnicity) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Response") %>%
  mutate(Measure = str_to_title(Measure),
         Response = replace_na(na_if(str_squish(Response), ""), "Missing")) %>%
  count(Measure, Response) %>%
  arrange(match(Measure, c("Gender", "Race", "Ethnicity")), desc(n), Response)

bind_rows(age.summary, category.summary) %>%
  mutate(Percent = scales::percent(n / n.participants, accuracy = 1),
         Measure = if_else(duplicated(Measure), "", Measure)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Measure", "Summary or response", "n", "% of sample"),
        caption = sprintf("Participant demographics (N = %d)", n.participants),
        table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"')
```

## Plots

### Plot of the top five properties for each category

```{r fig.height=6, fig.width=10, message=FALSE}
# As in Teleology and Generics, rank phrases by how often each category was
# selected. Rank all 40 phrases for each response, with alphabetical ties.
df.exp1.counts = df.exp1.long %>%
  count(item, response) %>%
  complete(item, response, fill = list(n = 0L))

df.exp1.ranked_items = df.exp1.counts %>%
  arrange(response, desc(n), item, .locale = "en") %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

df.exp1.top_items = df.exp1.ranked_items %>% filter(rank <= 5L)

# Keep the full distribution of responses for each selected phrase.
df.plot = df.exp1.counts %>%
  inner_join(df.exp1.top_items %>%
               rename(type = response) %>%
               select(-n),
             by = "item", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = categories),
         item.plot = paste(type, item, sep = "\n")) %>%
  filter(n > 0)

plot.exp1.top = ggplot(data = df.plot,
                      mapping = aes(x = reorder(item.plot, -rank),
                                    y = n,
                                    fill = response)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75,
           color = "black",
           position = position_fill(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("^[^\n]+\n", "", x),
                   expand = expansion(add = 0.55)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  coord_flip(expand = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~type, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Top five phrases for each category",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", drop = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
        text = element_text(size = 12),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(b = 8)),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 12, r = 25, b = 12, l = 15),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank())

plot.exp1.top

dir.create(params$figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(filename = file.path(params$figure_dir, "exp1_top_stacked.pdf"),
       plot = plot.exp1.top,
       height = 6,
       width = 10,
       device = cairo_pdf)
```

### Item selection

```{r exp1-top-five}
# Flag any item outside the top five that received as many votes as rank 5.
df.exp1.cutoff_ties = df.exp1.ranked_items %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  filter(n == n[5L], any(rank > 5L & n == n[5L])) %>%
  ungroup()

df.exp1.top_items %>%
  transmute(Category = response, Rank = rank, Phrase = item, Votes = n,
            Percent = scales::percent(n / n.participants, accuracy = 1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Top five phrases by number of votes for each category",
        table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-condensed"')

if (nrow(df.exp1.cutoff_ties) > 0L) {
  df.exp1.cutoff_ties %>%
    transmute(Category = response, Rank = rank, Phrase = item, Votes = n,
              Plotted = if_else(rank <= 5L, "Yes", "No")) %>%
    kable(caption = "Ties at the fifth-place cutoff (alphabetical order)",
          table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed"')
}
```
